context.requirement_text:
Second half of ISS-0431/GH#835's fix for its own stated PRIMARY
surface, atop REQ-216's core module. Mirrors REQ-186/REQ-187's and
REQ-214/REQ-215's own "core module first, wiring requirement(s)
second, disjoint files" split precedent in this file.

TWO ADMISSION GATES, NOT ONE, because tenant identity is not known
until partway through `Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline`'s existing chain --
read in full (lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex): `Plug.Parsers` runs
first, then `assign_trace_id`, then `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(which itself resolves tenant identity via a DB read -- token
verification, tenant-by-realm/slug resolution, JIT provisioning --
i.e. AuthPipeline's OWN work already consumes a DB connection BEFORE
any tenant identity exists to gate on), then
`Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`, then `match`/`dispatch`. Given that
ordering, a single per-tenant-only gate cannot run early enough to
cover AuthPipeline's own connection use. Resolved as follows, stated
as an accepted, disclosed limitation rather than silently glossed
over (matching this project's own honesty convention for a limitation
that cannot be fully closed within one requirement's scope, e.g.
decision 0014's own disclosed WASM native-crash gap):

1. GLOBAL gate, mounted FIRST in the chain -- before `Plug.Parsers`,
so a request rejected for lack of capacity is rejected before any
body-parsing work is spent on it. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global)`. Covers AuthPipeline's own
connection use (the gap named above) because it runs before
AuthPipeline and gates ALL downstream DB-connection-holding work,
auth included.
2. PER-TENANT gate, mounted immediately AFTER `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(tenant identity now resolved into `conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id`)
and BEFORE `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`/`match`/`dispatch`. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire({:tenant, schema_name})`, resolving
`schema_name` the same way `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus` and
`Letflow.Scheduler.Poller` already do (tenant-id -> schema-name
resolution already exists in this codebase; reuse it, do not
re-derive). Covers TenantStatus's own DB lookup and every sub-router's
dispatch work -- the dominant share of connection-holding time per
REQ-056/ISS-0431's own round-trip profiling.
DISCLOSED LIMITATION: AuthPipeline's own DB work (steps 1-4 of its
moduledoc) is covered by the global gate only, not a per-tenant one,
because tenant identity does not exist yet at that point in the
chain. This is accepted, not silently omitted -- state it in this
plug's own moduledoc.
3. Both gates: on `{:error, :capacity}`, respond immediately (halt the
plug chain, no further plugs run) via
`Letflow.Api.Response.service_unavailable/2` (REQ-066, ALREADY
EXISTING -- do not add a new response helper), with the
`Retry-After` header set explicitly on the conn first (matching
`Response.rate_limited/2`'s own documented "caller sets Retry-After"
convention) to a fixed, configured seconds value (config, default 1)
-- NOT a computed estimate, since this admission mechanism has no
queueing/backoff-timing model to estimate from (a fixed short value
matching `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`'s own existing `@retry_after_seconds
"30"` precedent's SHAPE, though the specific number here is
independently justified: admission rejection is a near-instant
decision with no wait queue behind it, unlike TenantStatus's
migration-in-progress case, so a MUCH shorter retry-after is
appropriate -- state this reasoning in the plug's moduledoc rather
than copying TenantStatus's 30-second value uncritically).
4. On success at BOTH gates: the plug stores both `admission_ref()`s
in `conn.assigns` and registers a `Plug.Conn.register_before_send/2`
(or equivalent, matching how this codebase already threads
request-scoped cleanup -- state which mechanism is chosen and why) or
calls `Letflow.Admission.release/1` for both refs when the response is
sent, so an admitted request's slot is freed exactly once, on every
response path including a request that raises inside a downstream
plug or router (verified in the acceptance criteria below).
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-216's core semaphore logic;
no change to `Letflow.Plugs.RateLimit` (still deferred, unmounted,
unrelated mechanism); no Poller wiring (REQ-218); no tier-weighted
per-tenant caps (REQ-216's own recorded open question).

task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (WF-02 Step 1b) re-check, rework iteration 1, on lib/letflow/design/req217-http-admission-wiring.md following CODE-DESIGNER's rework at step-01c. Verifying all four findings from step-01b's FAIL verdict are genuinely resolved, plus a full fresh read of the whole doc.
acceptance_criteria: with REQ-216's global cap artificially forced to 0 (test config override), every request to any /api/v1/* route -- including one that would otherwise pass auth -- receives HTTP 503 with a Retry-After header and Plug.Parsers never runs (no body-parsing side effect observable), confirmed by a request carrying a body too large for the parser's own limit still returning 503 rather than 413

with the global cap open but a specific tenant's per-tenant cap artificially forced to 0, a request authenticated as that tenant receives HTTP 503 with Retry-After, while a request authenticated as a DIFFERENT tenant (same global cap) succeeds -- both requests observed in the same test

a successfully admitted request that completes normally releases both its global and per-tenant admission_ref()s exactly once, verified by exhausting the cap, making one full round-trip request, and observing a subsequent request now succeeds

a successfully admitted request whose downstream handler RAISES still releases both admission_ref()s (no permanent slot leak on an error path) -- a test that forces a raise in a route handler and then verifies a subsequent request still succeeds

the 503 response body matches Letflow.Api.Response.service_unavailable/2's existing Error.service_unavailable/1 document shape exactly (same fields REQ-066's own test/letflow/api/error_test.exs already asserts), confirmed by comparing against that existing test's expected shape rather than asserting a new ad hoc body shape

the plug chain order change is confirmed by reading lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex: the global admission plug is the very first plug (before Plug.Parsers), and the per-tenant admission plug is positioned after Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline and before Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

checks_performed.point_1_crash_safety_trace: VERIFIED FIXED. Design §0 (lines 88-162) now correctly cites deps/plug/lib/plug/router.ex:254-271 and deps/plug/lib/plug/conn/wrapper_error.ex, matching what I independently read in both files. Confirmed accurate: Plug.Router's dispatch/2 wraps a raise from the matched route handler in Plug.Conn.WrapperError.reraise(conn, kind, reason, stacktrace), where `conn` is dispatch/2's own function parameter -- the fully-downstream conn carrying both admission-ref assigns. Confirmed accurate: Plug.ErrorHandler's generated call/2 (deps/plug/lib/plug/error_handler.ex) has a `rescue e in Plug.Conn.WrapperError` clause using e.conn (downstream, reliable) and a separate `catch kind, reason` clause using call/2's own outer parameter (pre-pipeline conn, unreliable) -- the design's §0 bullets and §5 correctly attribute Mechanism B's necessity only to the second, narrower case: a raise inside a plug running BEFORE dispatch/2 (AuthPipeline, TenantStatus, or Admission's own believed-unreachable branches), not a blanket 'nothing wraps in WrapperError' claim. Independently re-verified the 'no per-plug try/catch before dispatch' claim by reading deps/plug/lib/plug/builder.ex myself (not just accepting the rework's restatement): Plug.Builder.compile/3's generated pipeline body (see quote_plug/7 and its `case ... do %Plug.Conn{halted: true} -> ...; %Plug.Conn{} -> unquote(acc); other -> raise ...` construction) is a plain nested-call/case-match chain with NO try/catch or rescue anywhere in it -- only Plug.Router's dispatch/2 (generated separately, only wrapping the final route-handler call) and Plug.ErrorHandler's own call/2 override (wrapping the entire pipeline including dispatch) introduce any exception handling. This confirms the design's narrower claim is correct: a raise inside a pre-dispatch plug propagates straight up, unwrapped, to whichever try/catch/rescue sits outermost -- which in this design is Plug.ErrorHandler's own `catch` clause with the pre-pipeline conn.
checks_performed.point_2_process_dictionary_convention: VERIFIED FIXED. Design §5/§9 now define `@admission_refs_pdict_key`, value `{Letflow.Plugs.Admission, :admission_refs}`, as a named module attribute. Independently spot-checked lib/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api.ex and lib/letflow/engine/lua/platform.ex myself: both files use exactly this `{ModuleName, :purpose_atom}` tuple bound to a `@xxx_pdict_key` module attribute (host_api.ex: `@staged_writes_pdict_key {Letflow.Engine.Wasm.HostApi, :staged_writes}` at line 221, `@fail_signal_pdict_key {Letflow.Engine.Wasm.HostApi, :fail_signal}` at line 229; platform.ex: `@staged_writes_pdict_key {__MODULE__, :staged_writes}` at line 284), each read/written via Process.get/put/delete keyed on the attribute, not a bare inline atom. The design's new attribute matches this convention's shape exactly.
checks_performed.point_3_no_literal_code_sweep: VERIFIED FIXED. Grepped the entire design doc myself for: fenced code blocks (only two remain, lines 190-195 and 294-296, both containing @type/@spec declarations only -- no executable bodies, permitted per this project's design-doc convention); pipe operator `|>` (zero hits); `Process.put/get/delete` (zero hits); anonymous-function `fn`/`end` syntax (zero hits); `assign(` (one hit, line 21, which quotes existing auth_pipeline.ex source as cited evidence, not new design code); `halt(` as a literal call (zero hits -- only prose references to `Plug.Conn.halt/1` as a named function); literal `plug X, opts` mount declarations in §1/§7 (zero -- converted to prose per the rework's own report); `def`/`defp` (zero hits). The §3, §4, and §5 literal expressions flagged in the prior FAIL (the pipe expression, the register_before_send anonymous-function literal, the Process.put/get/delete lines, and handle_errors/2's full body) are all gone, replaced with numbered prose steps. §1's and §7's plug-mount code fences and §4's config keyword-list fence, which the rework's own report says it proactively cleaned beyond what was originally flagged, are confirmed also clean on independent re-check.
checks_performed.point_4_oq2_resolution: VERIFIED FIXED. §9 now states 'Resolved -- tenant-derivation-failure branches (was OQ-2 in an earlier version of this design)' explicitly, citing this validator's own step-01b determination that the crash-on-unreachable-branch choice is acceptable, matching TenantStatus's fail-closed precedent. Not left open. §9's closing line, 'No further open questions remain for this design,' is consistent with both the pdict convention and OQ-2 being resolved.
checks_performed.full_fresh_read_for_new_issues: Read the entire design doc end to end. No new ambiguity, TBD/deferral language, or literal code introduced by the rework beyond what points 1-4 already cover. §6's async-scope-boundary statement, §7's exact chain listing, and §8's moduledoc-obligation checklist are all still prose-only and unambiguous. Acceptance-criteria coverage from the prior review (AC1-AC6 each map to a design section; AC7 is a build/test-runner concern) is unaffected by the rework and still holds.

result.verdict_statement: PASS. All four rework points from step-01b are genuinely fixed, each independently re-verified against the underlying source (deps/plug/lib/plug/router.ex, deps/plug/lib/plug/conn/wrapper_error.ex, deps/plug/lib/plug/error_handler.ex, deps/plug/lib/plug/builder.ex, lib/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api.ex, lib/letflow/engine/lua/platform.ex), not merely accepted from the rework's own restatement. The crash-safety trace is now accurate and correctly scoped; the process-dictionary key follows this codebase's own established naming convention; a full independent sweep of the entire document found zero remaining literal executable Elixir outside the two permitted @type/@spec-only fences; OQ-2 is stated as resolved. Design is eligible for ELIXIR-DEV.
